driver: Work reaches a paid tier only when a volunteer tier falls short, and the volunteer tier's capacity shows only in the periods it fell short, since in every other period it handled everything that arrived; with almost no new volunteers arriving, each pool shrinks at a steady exit rate, so units whose records show almost nothing reaching the paid tier cross below their arrivals inside the forward window, while a share of arrivals carried forward, a trend in the paid work, or capacity read from recent throughput each misses the crossing.
driver_concrete: Every community review item at Quernstone goes first to the volunteer reviewers and reaches the paid moderators only if no volunteer has reviewed it 72 hours after it entered the inbox; volunteers review at their own pace when the inbox is full and below it when it runs dry, so their pace shows only in months when items were routed (every site in 2021 and 2022, Security, Embedded and Scientific Computing since late 2025), and since almost no members have reached the review privilege after autumn 2024 every site's pool shrinks by about two per cent a month, which takes Data & ML, Databases, DevOps and Game Development, with almost nothing routed since 2023, below their 2027 inbox arrivals.
stump: Carrying each site's paid queue hours per question over the last twelve months onto the 2027 question plan files a pool of about 105 FTE (about 110 to 114 with each site's routed share, its monthly paid hours or its reviewer pool trended forward), inside finance's 110-FTE envelope; the step that lands it there is treating routed items as a share of arrivals, when they are the arrivals each site's shrinking reviewer pool cannot review at the pace reviewers keep when the inbox is full, which puts four sites routed almost nothing since 2023 short of their 2027 arrivals and files about 130.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stacks the old monthly queue workbook and the new daily inbox export, maps the old site names to the new codes, and reads the charter's need definition, the 2027 standards and the 2027 question plan correctly carries each site's paid queue hours per question (or each queue's routed share) onto the plan and files about 105 FTE, or 110 to 114 with the routed share, the paid hours or the reviewer count trended; items reach the paid team only when the volunteers fall short, so each site's 2027 routed items are its 2027 arrivals less what its shrinking reviewer pool can review at the pace reviewers keep when the inbox is full, which files about 130.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each site's 2027 volunteer review capacity, forecast the way product analytics forecasts a user segment's retained activity (the reviewer pool projected from its own monthly exits and near-zero arrivals, times the activity each retained reviewer delivers when work is plentiful) and set against the 2027 inbox the plan implies; with another field's nouns (a hospital's agency nurses, a utility's call centre) there is no volunteer user cohort whose engagement decays on its own retention curve and whose output shows only when work outruns it, so the forecast that decides the call has nothing to stand on.
layer1: a review-platform change in January 2024: a monthly per-queue workbook for 2021 to 2023 (one sheet a year, the edit queue added in 2022) beside a daily inbox export by item type from 2024
site names in the old workbook against site codes in the new export, with Graphics folded into Game Development in 2023, mapped by the site register
UTC day boundaries in the platform exports against Toronto time in the moderation team's own records
the September 2026 inbox export pulled twice, a preliminary pull with the last three days' routing still open and a revised pull a week later
reviewer accounts re-keyed at the platform change, old site-local reviewer numbers mapped to network account ids

differentiation.task148: task148 drains a queue by abandonment and prices waits; here no item leaves on its own, the 72-hour hand-off is a routing rule, and the forecast is how many items the volunteers will not reach
